name: warp_distance
title: Distances from an origin, counted in period groups.

origin.description: Counts how many period groups separate each date from an origin.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A Date, POSIXct, or POSIXlt vector.

arguments.name: period
arguments.text: year, quarter, month, week, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond, yweek, mweek, yday, or mday.

arguments.name: every
arguments.text: How many periods share one group. A positive integer.

arguments.name: origin
arguments.text: The reference instant. NULL is 1970-01-01 00:00:00 in the time zone of x.

origin.details: Year, month, and day keep only that field of the origin. Quarter is a month group of every times 3. Week is a day group of every times 7. yday and yweek restart when the origin's month-day comes around again. mday and mweek restart on the first of each month. For a POSIXct, hour and the finer periods group absolute seconds, after trimming anything past microseconds. A Date is midnight UTC. If the time zones differ, x is relabeled with origin's zone and a warning is given; the seconds do not change.
origin.value: A double vector. Missing dates stay missing.

translation.description: Counts how many period groups separate each date from an origin.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A Date, POSIXct, or POSIXlt. Date is days since 1970-01-01. POSIXct is seconds since the UTC epoch.

arguments.name: period
arguments.text: The same period names as R.

arguments.name: every
arguments.text: How many periods share one group.

arguments.name: origin
arguments.text: The reference Date or POSIXct. None uses the epoch in x's time zone.

translation.details: The groups follow warp's calendar. zoneinfo supplies the civil date of a POSIXct. NumPy holds the double result. A mismatched time zone warns and relabels x.
translation.value: A float64 NumPy array. Missing values are NaN.
